title: Kunti
body:
Kunti

Kunti was born as Pritha to Surasena of the Yadava clan, and was the sister of Vasudeva, the father of Lord Krishna. Because her father's cousin, Kuntibhoja, was childless, Surasena gave his daughter Pritha in adoption to him, and she received the name Kunti.
When Kunti was a little girl, Sage Durvasa stayed as a guest in Kuntibhoja's palace. Highly pleased by her unwavering patience, devotion, and care, the sage granted her a divine mantra. He said: 'If you call upon any god repeating this mantra, that god will manifest himself and bless you with a son equal to him in glory.'
Out of innocent curiosity and youthful impatience, Kunti tested the mantra's efficacy then and there. Looking up at the heavens, she invoked Surya, the Sun God. Immediately, the sky darkened with clouds, and Surya stood before her. Terrified of public scandal, Kunti begged him to return, but Surya, bound by the mantra's power, blessed her with a child, assuring her that she would regain her virginity after childbirth.
Kunti gave birth to a radiant baby boy, who was born with sacred golden armour and earrings. Fearing public condemnation, she placed the baby in a sealed straw basket and set it afloat on the Yamuna. The basket was found by Adhiratha, the charioteer of Dhritarashtra, who was childless. He and his wife Radha raised the child as their own, naming him Karna. Later, Kuntibhoja held a Swayamvara for Kunti, at which Kunti placed the marriage garland on the neck of King Pandu.
